While Citi also consolidates VIEs when it is the primary beneficiary, its disclosed candidates do not specifically address the municipal bond or resecuritization trust topic or the specific residual interest/securities retention consolidation criteria for such trusts that are central to BAC's disclosure.

Goldman Sachs' candidates focus on investment funds structured as limited partnerships/LLCs (typically voting interest entities) and general VIE primary beneficiary determination. These do not specifically address the municipal bond or resecuritization trust consolidation policies, nor the specific residual interest dynamics for municipal trusts described in BAC's disclosure.

comparisons.peer_topic: Consolidation of Non-Customer TOB Trusts as VIEs
comparisons.peer_summary: TOB trusts are classified as variable interest entities (VIEs), and the Firm consolidates non-customer TOB trusts because it holds the residual interest, granting it the power to direct significant economic activities and the obligation to absorb losses or right to receive benefits.
comparisons.comparison: Both BAC and JPM disclose specific consolidation policies for municipal bond trusts (BAC: municipal bond/resecuritization trusts; JPM: TOB trusts). Both firms consolidate these entities when they hold the residual interest, which grants them the power to direct significant economic activities and the obligation to absorb potentially significant losses or receive benefits. BAC states it consolidates if it has sole discretion over design and retains securities/commitments, while JPM explicitly states it consolidates non-customer TOB trusts because as the Residual holder, it has the right to make decisions impacting economic performance and bear losses/benefits.

sentences.text: The Corporation consolidates a municipal bond or resecuritization trust if it has control over the ongoing activities of the trust such as the remarketing of the trust's liabilities or, if there are no ongoing activities, sole discretion over the design of the trust, including the identification of securities to be transferred in and the structure of securities to be issued, and also retains securities or has liquidity or other commitments that could potentially be significant to the trust.

The Firm consolidates non-customer TOB trusts because as the Residual holder, the Firm has the right to make decisions that significantly impact the economic performance of the municipal bond vehicle, and it has the right to receive benefits and bear losses that could potentially be significant to the municipal bond vehicle.

comparisons.peer_topic: Firm's alternative role and consolidation criteria in MTOB trusts
comparisons.peer_summary: The Firm may extend a temporary loan to the trust instead of purchasing securities for remarketing and consolidates any trust in which it holds the residual interest.
comparisons.comparison: Both BAC and MS disclose consolidation criteria for municipal bond/trust structures involving residual interests. BAC consolidates municipal bond trusts if it retains securities or commitments that could be significant. MS consolidates municipal tender option bond trusts specifically in which it holds the residual interest. Both identify the retention of significant economic interest (securities/commitments or residual) as a key driver for consolidation when the firm has control or power over the trust.
